record.paper_title: Open problems on regular languages: an historical perspective
record.context_brief: Largest proper positive lp-variety closed under shuffle
record.original_question: Consider positive lp-varieties of languages, meaning lp-varieties that are not required to be closed under complement. Is there a largest proper positive lp-variety of languages that is closed under the shuffle product?

evidence.quote:
Is there a largest proper positive lp-variety of languages
closed under shuffle?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Fix a finite alphabet framework: for each finite alphabet $A$, let $A^*$ denote the free monoid of words on $A$. A class $\mathcal{V}$ assigning to every finite alphabet $A$ a set $\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ of regular languages of $A^*$ is called a positive lp-variety of languages if:
(i) for every $A$, $\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ is closed under finite unions and finite intersections (positive Boolean operations, but not necessarily under complementation);
(ii) $\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ is closed under left and right quotients by words;
(iii) $\mathcal{V}$ is closed under inverses of length-preserving morphisms, i.e. if $\varphi : A^* \to B^*$ is a morphism with $|\varphi(a)|=1$ for all $a\in A$, then $L\in\mathcal{V}(B^*)$ implies $\varphi^{-1}(L)\in\mathcal{V}(A^*)$.
A positive lp-variety $\mathcal{V}$ is proper if it is not the class of all regular languages. The shuffle product of two languages $L_1,L_2\subseteq A^*$ is
$$L_1\shuffle L_2 \;=\; \{\, u_1 v_1 u_2 v_2 \cdots u_n v_n \;:\; n\ge 1,\; u_1\cdots u_n\in L_1,\; v_1\cdots v_n\in L_2,\; u_i,v_i\in A^*\,\}.$$
A positive lp-variety $\mathcal{V}$ is closed under shuffle if $L_1,L_2\in\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ implies $L_1\shuffle L_2\in\mathcal{V}(A^*)$ for every $A$.

Question. Does there exist a largest proper positive lp-variety of languages that is closed under the shuffle product? Equivalently, is there a proper positive lp-variety $\mathcal{W}$, closed under shuffle, such that every proper positive lp-variety of languages closed under shuffle is contained in $\mathcal{W}$?
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that there is a largest proper positive variety of languages W closed under shuffle (in the classical sense, closed under inverses of all morphisms), characterized via ordered monoids. However, the question as posed concerns positive lp-varieties (closed only under inverses of length-preserving morphisms), a strictly weaker closure condition for which the analogous existence result does not appear in the located references. No definitive published resolution for the lp-variety version was found.

status_evidence.title: Shuffle on positive varieties of languages
status_evidence.snippet: The largest proper positive variety of languages closed under shuffle is characterized via an ordered-monoid identity on mutually inverse elements.
status_evidence.claim: For positive varieties (with full inverse-morphism closure) the largest proper such variety closed under shuffle exists and is described.

status_evidence.title: Shuffle product of regular languages: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists open questions concerning shuffle closure of positive varieties.
status_evidence.claim: The lp-variety version of the question is listed among open problems.
